relationship: Opening workloads and advancing the clock connects RAM, cache and drive settings to latency, pressure and faults.

learnerLoop.action: Configure memory, open or close work apps, then step or run the clock.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The simulated workload, memory pressure and access path change.
learnerLoop.evidence: Metrics, desktop, architecture panel and log expose timing and fault consequences.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Change the workload or configuration to explain the observed performance.

invariants: Metrics and log entries describe the active simulated configuration and workload.
Closing an app removes its associated simulated memory demand.
safeAdaptations: Change application stories, parameter values or guidance while retaining observable memory hierarchy consequences.
nonGoals: Measuring or managing the learner's actual computer memory.

task.description: Workload comparison goal and selectable memory/storage configuration.
task.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

controls.description: Boot/advance the machine and create or close workloads.
controls.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

model.description: Interactive desktop beside storage, page file, RAM and cache; current and next queued memory actions remain paired.
model.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

evidence.description: Cache hits, page faults and memory pressure; compact current/next cycle-progress bars; causal OS log beneath the desktop.
evidence.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

cycles.domain: Each gate advances up to 10 cycles; action latency follows the current teaching configuration.

memory.description: Allocated physical memory and page-file blocks.
memory.domain: 16, 32 or 48 RAM blocks representing 4, 8 or 12 GB.

latency.domain: L1 1, L2 5, L3 14, RAM 45 cycles; storage and page-file transfers are longer.
latency.output: Current action, latency reference and simulation/hardware comparison.

modes.configuration: Three RAM sizes, three cache configurations, SSD/HDD, five clock animation speeds.
modes.workload: Boot, open work apps, stress memory and close background apps, plus desktop application interactions.
modes.support: Open simulation without Working, exam toggle or terminal score.

dependencies: Starting the clock loads the OS before workload shortcuts become available.
Allocation and access events update the hierarchy, queued work, metrics and decision log.
Configuration changes reset the simulation. Temporary fallback accesses preserve the learner-selected foreground application.
The first opened desktop application dismisses the shared icon introduction across subsequent redraws.
Core evidence distinguishes cache/RAM reads, waiting for a page fault, and OS page management; edge-anchored paths resize with the devices.
implementation.completion: No terminal gate; learners compare access routes and memory pressure over repeated workloads.
limitations: Relative teaching latencies and approximate hardware comparison are simplified rather than hardware benchmarks.
Desktop process identities remain aligned with allocated block colours.

Cache entries are page-level teaching proxies. OS page-management operations do not simulate their own instruction fetches; foreground application accesses can displace OS cache references while OS pages remain resident in RAM.
